applicableAreas: Buildings 7 and 8 on southern boundary adjacent to OHE line
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) depicts an overhead electric line (OHE) routing along and crossing the site. Sheet 9 (Proposed Site Plan) shows this OHE line running along the southern boundary of the property. Buildings 7 and 8 are positioned closest to this southern boundary. However, no clearance dimension lines or annotations are provided on either the site plan or any building elevation sheets showing the horizontal distance from the buildings' exterior walls or projections to the OHE conductor. No profile/section views are provided showing vertical clearances. The plans do not identify whether the OHE line is a primary, secondary, or neutral conductor, nor is there a surveyed elevation of the conductor provided. No dimension callouts originate from the conductor location itself—the critical measurement baseline required by code.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires buildings to maintain minimum 7.5 feet horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead electric conductors. This measurement must be from the outside conductor, not from the pole. The applicant has not provided evidence that this clearance is maintained. Without (1) building elevation sheets showing surveyed conductor elevations, (2) dimension annotations from the outside conductor to the building face, or (3) a registered surveyor's proximity survey per UCM § 1.10.3, the reviewer cannot determine whether the requirement is met. The conservative approach is to flag this as unclear pending submittal of required elevation documentation and proximity survey data.
findings.comment: No building elevation sheets or dimension callouts showing 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from outside conductor to Buildings 7 and 8. Provide registered surveyor elevation data and clearance dimension annotations.

applicableAreas: Parking areas and site features on southern portion near OHE line
findings.observation: Sheet 4 shows existing OHE line with associated utility poles. Sheet 9 shows the same OHE line routing along the southern boundary with parking areas, driveways, and site improvements in close proximity. The plans do not specify whether the overhead line serves distribution or transmission function, nor are the conductor types (primary, neutral, secondary) identified. No dimension annotations are provided showing distances from site facilities (parking, driveways, retaining walls) to the outside conductor. A registered surveyor proximity survey documenting existing and proposed facility locations relative to the OHE line is not provided.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires customer facilities (parking, driveways, site improvements) to maintain 15-foot radial clearance from outside conductors of overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. The distinction between distribution and transmission affects the applicable clearance standard. Without a registered surveyor proximity survey showing the conductor type, voltage level, and radial distances from all proposed facilities, compliance cannot be verified. The applicant has not submitted this required documentation.
findings.comment: No registered surveyor proximity survey provided showing distances from proposed parking areas and site features to outside conductor of OHE line. Provide proximity survey documenting radial clearances from all customer facilities.

applicableAreas: Building 8 roof and overhang areas adjacent to southern OHE line
findings.observation: Sheet 9 shows Building 8 positioned adjacent to the southern boundary where the OHE line is routed. However, no building elevation or section views are provided on the site plan set that show the roof elevation of Building 8, any rooftop projections (overhangs, canopies, HVAC penetrations, vents), or their vertical clearance from the overhead line. No profile sections are provided showing the relationship between building projections and the conductor location. Building height is specified as 36'-1" but the finished floor and roof elevations are not dimensioned relative to the OHE line.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires both 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance (horizontal) and implies vertical clearance verification for any building projections. Without profile or elevation sheets showing the surveyed conductor elevation and the building roof/overhang elevation dimensioned relative to that conductor, compliance cannot be determined. The applicant must provide elevation views with clearance dimensions for all building projections near the overhead line.
findings.comment: No building elevation or profile sheets provided showing vertical clearances from Building 8 roof and overhangs to overhead electric line. Provide engineered building elevations with surveyed conductor elevation and clearance dimension annotations.

applicableAreas: Buildings 7 and 8 adjacent to southern OHE line; entire site with overhead facilities
findings.observation: No building elevation sheets are included in the 39-sheet site plan set. The README index lists sheets 1-39 as site/civil engineering and landscape drawings, with no architectural elevation sheets shown. Existing overhead electric lines are depicted on Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions) and Sheet 9 (Proposed Site Plan), but no surveyed conductor elevation data is provided on any sheet. No registered surveyor's mid-span clearance measurements are documented. The electrical survey required by Austin Energy Design per UCM § 1.10.3 does not appear to have been submitted.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 explicitly requires that surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors be included on building elevation sheets to demonstrate required clearances are met. The applicant has not submitted any building elevation sheets. This is a mandatory documentation requirement for any site with buildings within clearance distance of overhead electric facilities. The absence of this required documentation constitutes a deficiency regardless of actual clearances that might exist on the ground.
findings.comment: Building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor elevations are missing. Provide building elevation drawings showing surveyed conductor locations and clearance dimensions to all building faces and projections.

applicableAreas: Buildings 7 and 8; parking areas; all structures within clearance distance of OHE line
findings.observation: No section or profile view exhibits are provided showing dimensions from the outer electric conductor to the outermost edge of buildings and site improvements. Sheet 9 (Proposed Site Plan) shows the OHE line and buildings in plan view only, without any profile views. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows contours and building FFEs but does not show overhead conductor elevation or clearance dimensions. No enlarged plan details with cross-section views have been submitted showing the relationship between conductors and building edges, parking surfaces, or driveways.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires dimension lines from the outer conductor to outermost building edges in plan and section views to verify clearance compliance. These dimension annotations are mandatory and must originate from the actual conductor location, not from the pole. The complete absence of section and profile exhibits with clearance dimensions is a deficiency. The applicant must provide these required exhibits.
findings.comment: No section/profile exhibits provided showing clearance dimensions from outer conductor to buildings and site features. Provide detailed section and plan views with dimension callouts from outside conductor to building edges and site improvements.

applicableAreas: Internal driveways and parking areas on southern portion of site where OHE line is routed
findings.observation: Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows finished floor elevations and site contours but does not provide finished driveway grade elevations at specific locations relative to the OHE line shown on Sheet 9. No section views are provided showing the vertical relationship between the lowest point of the overhead electric line and the finished grade of parking/drive areas. Truck traffic classification (which determines 16-foot vs. 18-foot clearance requirement) is not specified on the plans. No mid-span clearance measurements from a registered surveyor are provided.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.6.2 requires minimum 16-foot vertical clearance for parking without truck traffic, or 18-foot with truck traffic, from the lowest point of overhead electric facilities (including service drops and telecommunications attachments). Without (1) documented finished grade elevations at driveway locations, (2) surveyed overhead line heights, and (3) specification of truck traffic usage, compliance cannot be verified. The applicant must provide site/utility profile views with documented vertical clearances.
findings.comment: No documented vertical clearance from finished driveway grades to overhead electric line. Provide grading plan section views with finished elevations at OHE line crossing and surveyed conductor height; specify truck traffic classification.

applicableAreas: All locations with clearance dimensions shown on overhead electric facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 9 shows the OHE line on the southern boundary of the site but includes NO dimension callouts or clearance annotations of any kind. Wherever clearance dimensions should appear (from conductor to buildings, parking, driveways), none are provided. The few dimension lines visible on Sheet 9 relate to building setbacks and site distances, not to overhead line clearances. The critical requirement to show dimension lines originating from the outside conductor location (not pole centerline) is therefore not met—because no dimensions are shown at all.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires clearance dimensions to be measured from the outside conductor, never from the utility pole centerline. On multi-conductor installations, the conductor may be several feet offset from pole center, creating significant measurement errors if pole-based dimensions are used. The applicant has not provided any clearance dimensions from any overhead electric infrastructure. This is a foundational deficiency—without dimension callouts originating from the conductor, the plans cannot communicate or verify clearance compliance.
findings.comment: No clearance dimensions are shown on site plans, measured from outside conductor as required. All clearance dimensions must originate from the actual conductor location, with notation showing measurement source.

applicableAreas: Buildings 7 and 8; parking and driveway areas adjacent to southern OHE line
findings.observation: Sheet 4 shows an existing OHE line with utility poles routed across the property. Sheet 9 shows Buildings 7 and 8 and parking/driveway areas positioned immediately adjacent to this overhead line (on southern boundary). Without seeing surveyed conductor elevations or documented clearance measurements, the vertical clearance appears potentially marginal—the minimum required clearances (7.5-foot sky-to-ground, 16-18-foot for driveways, 7.5-foot for parking) cannot be visually confirmed from plan-view drawings alone. No mid-span clearance survey data from a registered surveyor is provided to document actual measured clearances.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires a registered surveyor's mid-span clearance measurements when existing overhead facilities may not meet minimum vertical clearance requirements or when visual determination is insufficient. Given the close proximity of buildings and parking to the OHE line shown on the plans, and the complete absence of vertical clearance documentation, a registered surveyor's measurement is required to verify compliance. The applicant has not provided this required survey work.
findings.comment: No registered surveyor mid-span clearance measurements provided despite buildings and parking areas being positioned adjacent to overhead electric line. Provide licensed surveyor measurements of overhead conductor heights and clearances to all proposed structures and site features.

applicableAreas: Southern boundary landscaping area with overhead electric line; mitigation tree plantings
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) depicts an overhead electric line (OHE) running along the southern boundary. Multiple mitigation trees (labeled 'M' on the plan) are positioned directly along this southern boundary, within or immediately adjacent to (less than 10 feet lateral distance from) the overhead line. Sheet 32 (Tree List) identifies the surveyed existing trees with species and Appendix F designation (Y/N/I), but does NOT specify the species of the proposed MITIGATION trees shown as 'M' symbols on Sheet 31. No legend or note on Sheet 31 provides species names for the mitigation plantings. No reference to ECM Appendix F Utility Compatible trees (UC designation) appears in the landscape legend. No clearance distance annotations or notes document the required 10-foot lateral separation or specify that utility-compatible species are being used.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires trees proposed within 50 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors to be from the Utility Compatible tree list in ECM Appendix F (generally species with mature height ≤20 feet marked 'UC'). The applicant's landscape plan shows mitigation trees under the overhead line but does not identify the species. Without species identification, the reviewer cannot verify that utility-compatible trees are being used. The vegetation plan is deficient. The applicant must identify all mitigation tree species and confirm they meet the UC requirements, OR relocate trees to comply with the 10-foot minimum lateral separation for non-utility-compatible species.
findings.comment: Mitigation trees shown on landscape plan adjacent to overhead electric line lack species identification and utility-compatible designation. Identify all mitigation tree species and confirm UC (Utility Compatible) status per ECM Appendix F, or relocate trees to maintain 10-foot minimum lateral clearance from outside conductor.

findings.observation: Sheet 1 (Cover Sheet) and Sheet 3 (General Notes) have been reviewed. Block 14 of Sheet 3 contains Austin Energy requirements addressing maintenance of clearances per NESC and OSHA but is phrased as developer responsibility language. The specific requirement per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003 for owner/contractor to notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines is not clearly called out as a discrete note on the cover sheet or title block. Blocks 14 and 20 of Sheet 3 reference general clearance responsibilities but the explicit 48-hour notification notice with contact information is not visibly highlighted or separated as a specific callout.
findings.reasoning: Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752 Section 752.003 requires notification to Austin Energy 48 hours before work near overhead electric lines. This requirement must be conspicuously noted on site plans. While general Austin Energy notes are present on Sheet 3, the specific 48-hour notification requirement is not clearly set out as a distinct, stand-alone note with notification procedures. Best practice is to include this as a separate, highlighted note on the cover sheet with contact information for Austin Energy notification.
findings.comment: Specific 48-hour notification note required by Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752 is not clearly called out on cover sheet or plans. Add conspicuous note: 'Owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before beginning any work near overhead electric lines. Contact [Austin Energy contact information].'
